mainTopic: Why an offering slaughtered with no stated intent (סתמא) is valid but a גט written סתמא is not, and the sources for each rule
overview: The גמרא finishes reading the פסוק about vows. A נדר that was not offered properly becomes a נדבה, and you may not change the intent of a נדבה, so the remaining steps must still be done properly. Then רבינא tells רב פפא about a contradiction רבא raised. From our משנה it seems that an offering slaughtered with no stated intent (סתמא) counts as לשמן, but a גט written סתמא is פסול. רבא answers that an offering already stands for its own purpose, while a wife does not stand ready for divorce. The גמרא then looks for the source that סתמא is valid for offerings. Proofs from the wording of our משנה and from both clauses of the משנה about פסח and שלמים are each pushed off. The working proof comes from רבי יוסי: בית דין told people not to state their intent, and the court would never set up a practice that ruins a קרבן. Finally, the גמרא looks for the source that a סתמא גט is פסול. The case of scribes in the market is rejected using רב פפא, and a new proof from the next part of that משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse calls it a gift, but it is a vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a difficulty in the פסוק: it calls the offering a נדבה, but it is really a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a vow offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of reading a פסוק. It asks why the פסוק calls this offering a נדבה (gift) when it is clearly a נדר (vow).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about keeping what you vowed, so the offering is a נדר. Calling it a נדבה looks like the wrong word. This oddity sets up the explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow offering. You say 'I take upon myself to bring an offering,' so you are obligated until you bring one.
A gift offering. You say 'this animal is an offering,' so there is no ongoing obligation.

phrases.english: It is a vow offering!
phrases.notes: This still refers to דברים 23:24, which uses the word 'נדבה' even though it's talking about a vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation from the פסוק that began just before this text.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is about a vow, so calling the offering a gift seems out of place.

steps.title: A vow offering done wrongly becomes a gift offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means this: if you offered it properly, it counts as your נדר. If not, it becomes only a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse means: if you did as you vowed, it is a vow offering. If not, it is a gift offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty. The word נדבה tells us what happens to a vow offering that was not brought properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering brought the right way fulfills the owner's vow. If it was done wrongly, it is still a valid offering, but now it is only a נדבה, and the owner still owes his vow. So the strange word נדבה teaches a new rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As you vowed, meaning offered properly

phrases.english: Rather, if you did as you vowed,
it shall be a vow offering,
and if not, it shall be a gift offering;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word נדבה seemed to be the wrong word for a vow offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow offering that was not done properly turns into a נדבה.

steps.title: You may not deviate with a gift offering either
steps.stepSummary: Once the offering is a נדבה, it still must be brought properly, because nobody may change the intent of a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is one allowed to deviate with a gift offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof with a question that answers itself. Of course you may not deviate with a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after one step was done with the wrong intent, the offering is still a real נדבה. Just as you may not start a נדבה with the wrong intent, you may not finish this one with the wrong intent. So the rest of the steps must be done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it permitted? (often a question that expects 'no')
To change or deviate, meaning to do it for the wrong purpose

steps.whatToRemember: An offering that no longer counts for its owner still has the status of a נדבה, so every remaining step must be done for its proper purpose.

phrases.english: And is it permitted to deviate with a gift offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading from step 2 to finish the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even after one step was done with the wrong intent, the remaining steps must still be done properly, just as with any נדבה.

steps.title: רבינא tells רב פפא about רבא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב פפא that רבא raised a contradiction between two excellent teachings and resolved it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב פפא: You were not with us last night in the area of בי חרמך, where רבא set two fine teachings against each other and reconciled them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. This step sets up what comes next: רבא's contradiction between two important sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. We only learn that רבא found two sources that seem to clash, and that he settled the clash. The next steps tell us what those sources are.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets one source against another, pointing out a contradiction
And resolves it, showing they do not really clash
The שבת boundary area of a town

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Pappa:
You were not with us last night
within the Shabbat limit of Bei Ḥarmakh,
where Rava set superior teachings against each other,
and resolved them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic that is not tied to the previous proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא found a contradiction between two important sources and resolved it.

steps.title: Which teachings were they?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which two fine teachings רבא contrasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are these superior teachings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for details about what רבינא described. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 only told us that a contradiction existed. This question asks for the actual sources, so we can see the clash for ourselves.

phrases.english: What are these superior teachings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the teaching mentioned in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which two sources did רבא contrast?

steps.title: First source: no stated intent counts as proper intent
steps.stepSummary: From our משנה, רבא learns that an offering slaughtered with no stated intent (סתמא) fulfills the owner's obligation. So סתמא counts as לשמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: all offerings slaughtered not for their own sake, and so on. The reason they do not count is that they were slaughtered for the wrong purpose. But if they were slaughtered with no stated intent, they do count for the owner's obligation. So no stated intent is treated like proper intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first side of רבא's contradiction. It makes an inference from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says offerings do not count for the owner only when slaughtered שלא לשמן. Since only that case is singled out, an offering slaughtered with no stated intent must count. This shows that סתמא is treated like לשמן; the second source, still to come, will seem to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for their own sake, meaning with the wrong purpose in mind
With no stated intent at all

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself never mentions סתמא. The rule about סתמא is רבא's inference from the wording 'שלא לשמן'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole contradiction. Next, the גמרא will bring a source that seems to treat סתמא as not good enough.

phrases.english: We learned: All slaughtered offerings
that were slaughtered not for their sake, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of our משנה: the offerings are fit but do not count for the owner's obligation.

phrases.english: The reason is that they were not for their sake;
but without specified intent,
they also count for the owner's obligation;
evidently, without specified intent is also like for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: כׇּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁנִּזְבְּחוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by giving the first of the two teachings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first teaching is our משנה. Its wording shows that סתמא counts like לשמן.

steps.title: The contradiction from a bill of divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets against our משנה a משנה about a גט, which says that a גט written with no stated intent is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he raised a contradiction: Any גט written not for the sake of the woman is invalid. So one written with no stated intent is also invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the second of the two 'fine teachings'. It is a משנה about a גט, and it seems to clash with what we just learned about offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For offerings, no stated intent is treated like proper intent (step 6). For a גט, no stated intent counts as invalid. Both cases are about acting 'for the sake of' something, so why are they treated differently?

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised a contradiction against it

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction:
Any bill of divorce that was written
not for the sake of the woman is invalid.
And one with no stated intent is also invalid!
phrases.notes: These words are not part of the quoted line. רבא is pointing out what that משנה holds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second teaching, which seems to contradict the first one from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that סתמא counts as לשמן for offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a גט, no stated intent makes it invalid. So 'no intent' should not count as proper intent for offerings either.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written with no stated intent is invalid

steps.title: Offerings stand for their purpose, a wife does not stand for divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that an offering's natural destiny is to be brought for its own purpose, but a wife's natural state is not to be divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it: Offerings, with no stated intent, stand for their own sake. A woman, in her ordinary state, does not stand ready for divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two cases have different starting points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an animal is set aside as a certain offering, it is already 'heading' toward that use. So saying nothing is the same as saying its proper name. A married woman is not heading toward divorce, so a גט must be written specifically for her.

keyTerms.meaning: They stand, meaning they are set and designated

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that an object follows its default purpose unless told otherwise, explains why silence is enough for offerings.

phrases.english: And he resolved:
Offerings, with no stated intent, stand for their own sake;
a woman, in her ordinary state,
does not stand ready for divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offerings and a גט should follow the same rule about no stated intent
steps.terutzMaskana: An offering's default is its own purpose, but a woman's default is not divorce, so silence works only for offerings

steps.title: Where do we learn that offerings with no intent are valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that offerings slaughtered with no stated intent are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that offerings with no stated intent are valid, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants to see where the rule rests in the text, and it sets up the search that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said our משנה teaches this rule. Now the גמרא wants to pin down exactly which wording proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And that offerings with no stated intent are valid,
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the contradiction is settled, asks for the source of the basic rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual source showing that סתמא is valid for offerings

steps.title: First try: the wording of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the proof comes from our משנה's wording, 'slaughtered not for their sake,' instead of 'not slaughtered for their sake.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is from what we learned: 'All offerings that were slaughtered not for their sake, etc.,' and it does not say 'that were not slaughtered for their sake'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first proof from the exact wording of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Slaughtered not for their sake' sounds like he actively said a wrong name. 'Not slaughtered for their sake' would also cover saying nothing at all. Since the משנה chose the first wording, it seems that only a wrong intent is a problem, and silence is fine.

phrases.english: If you say it is from what we learned:
All offerings that were slaughtered
not for their sake, etc.
and it does not teach
"that were not slaughtered for their sake";
phrases.notes: This second wording would include an offering slaughtered with no intent at all. The משנה avoided it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 9
steps.raayaObject: That סתמא is valid for offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'שנזבחו שלא לשמן' in our משנה

steps.title: The same wording appears for a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first proof, because the גט משנה uses the same wording and yet a גט with no stated intent is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding a גט too, it teaches: 'Any גט that was written not for the sake of the woman is invalid,' and it does not teach 'that was not written for the sake of the woman is invalid'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 10 by pointing to the identical wording in the גט משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט משנה also says 'written not for her sake,' yet we know a גט with no stated intent is invalid (step 7). So this style of wording proves nothing about silence.

phrases.english: Regarding a bill of divorce too, it teaches:
Any bill of divorce that was written
not for the sake of the woman is invalid
and it does not teach
"that was not written for the sake of the woman is invalid"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 10
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same wording appears for a גט, where סתמא is invalid, so the wording cannot show that סתמא is valid

steps.title: Second try: פסח and then no intent is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove the rule from a משנה that invalidates 'for a פסח and for שלמים', which implies that 'for a פסח and then no intent' is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from what we learned: 'How is for its sake and then not for its sake? For the sake of a פסח and then for the sake of שלמים.' The reason it is invalid is that he said פסח and then שלמים. But פסח and then no stated intent is valid. So no stated intent is like for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source for the rule, using a careful reading of a later משנה. The next step pushes this proof off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's example of 'for its sake and not for its sake' needed him to actually say a wrong name (שלמים). So if he started with פסח and then said nothing, the offering stays valid. That shows silence counts like the proper intent.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from what we learned:
How is it "for its sake and not for its sake"?
For the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a peace offering.
The reason it is invalid is that he said
for the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a peace offering,
but for the sake of a Paschal offering and then with no stated intent, it is valid;
apparently, no stated intent is like for their own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a working one
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Source that סתמא is valid for offerings
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the משנה 'כיצד לשמן ושלא לשמן', which implies that פסח followed by סתמא is valid

steps.title: The first case had a correct starting intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from 'for a פסח and for שלמים'. There, he began with correct intent, and a person acts according to his first intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that case is different, because the משנה holds that whoever does an action does it with his original intent in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 12. In that case, the person started out saying 'for a פסח', so we can't learn anything about a case with no intent at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 reasoned that 'for a פסח, then no intent' is valid, so no intent must be fine. The rejection says the second, silent part is valid only because it is carried along by his first stated intent of פסח. In a true סתם case there is no first intent to lean on, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; used to push off a proof
He acts according to his original intent

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that סתם is invalid. It is only saying this case cannot prove that סתם is valid.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case from Step 12: 'for a פסח and for שלמים'.

phrases.english: since it says: anyone who performs an action
performs it with his original intent in mind!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה – עַל דַּעַת רִאשׁוֹנָה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the רישא, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the רישא there was a correct first intent that carries over. A true סתם case has no such intent.

steps.title: A new proof from the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the סיפא: 'for שלמים and then for a פסח' is invalid only because the first intent was wrong. So 'no intent, then for a פסח' must be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from the latter clause: 'not for their sake and then for their sake', meaning for the sake of שלמים and then for the sake of a פסח. The reason it is invalid is that he said 'for שלמים' and then 'for a פסח'. But if he started with no intent and then said 'for a פסח', it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof, this time from the second clause of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the silent part comes first, so it cannot lean on an earlier correct intent. The משנה blames the wrong first intent (שלמים) for the problem. That implies a silent start followed by פסח is fine, so סתם alone does no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; moving to a new attempt
The latter clause of a משנה
The reason is; sets up an inference

phrases.english: Rather, learn it from the latter clause:
'not for their sake and then for their sake'
meaning for the sake of a peace offering and then for the sake of a Paschal offering.
The reason it is invalid is that he said
'for a peace offering' and then 'for a Paschal offering'
but with no intent and then for a Paschal offering, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רישא proof failed, tries the סיפא of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a קרבן slaughtered with no stated intent is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: 'for שלמים and for a פסח' is invalid, which implies 'סתם and for a פסח' is valid.

steps.title: The final intent may show what he meant at the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the סיפא proof. There, his final intent of פסח reveals that his silent start was also meant for a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that case is different, because the משנה holds that his ending proves what his beginning was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silent start in the סיפא may be valid only because his later words 'for a פסח' show that he meant פסח all along. A completely silent slaughter has no such later words to explain it. So the proof doesn't reach a true סתם case.

keyTerms.meaning: His end proves what his beginning was

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
since it says: his end proves what his beginning was!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר: יוֹכִיחַ סוֹפוֹ עַל תְּחִילָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the סיפא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The silent start there is explained by his final correct intent. A true סתם case has nothing to explain it.

steps.title: The wording may just match the first clause
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: the סיפא may be worded 'not for their sake and for their sake' only to match the רישא, so no inference can be drawn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, since the משנה taught 'for their sake and not for their sake', it also taught 'not for their sake and for their sake'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason to reject the proof from the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 14 depended on the exact wording of the סיפא. Here the גמרא says the תנא may have chosen that wording only to mirror the רישא. If so, the wording is not precise enough to learn anything about סתם, and the search for a source continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he taught (the first case, he taught the second to match)

steps.whatToRemember: Both clauses of the משנה (פסח and then שלמים, or שלמים and then פסח) fail as proofs that a סתם slaughter is valid. Each case has a stated correct intent, at the start or at the end, that could explain why the silent part is valid.

phrases.english: Alternatively, since the תנא taught
'for their sake and then not for their sake',
he also taught 'not for their sake and then for their sake'!
phrases.notes: In other words, the second clause is worded this way just to match the first, so we can't read a lesson into its wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent rejection of the proof from Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the סיפא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording of the סיפא may only mirror the רישא, so it is not precise enough to support an inference.

steps.title: A new proof from the six intentions of slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source, a later משנה listing six intentions for slaughtering a זבח. In that משנה, רבי יוסי says it is כשר even without any of them, because of a תנאי בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from this משנה: an offering is slaughtered for the sake of six things: for the sake of the offering, the owner, ה׳, the altar fires, the aroma, and the pleasing. A חטאת and an אשם are also slaughtered for the sake of the sin. רבי יוסי said: even if he had none of these in mind, it is כשר, because it is a stipulation of בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier proofs failed, so the גמרא tries a new source: a משנה about the six intentions for slaughtering. This step quotes the source. The next steps explain it and draw the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key part is רבי יוסי's line: even with no intention at all, the offering is כשר. That is exactly the case of סתמא. The words 'תנאי בית דין' are explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Six things, the six intentions one should have when slaughtering
A stipulation or rule set by the court
For the sake of the sin it atones for

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found later in this מסכת, on 46b.

phrases.english: For the sake of six things the offering is slaughtered:
for the sake of the offering, for the sake of the one offering it,
for the sake of the Name, for the sake of the fires,
for the sake of an aroma, for the sake of pleasing.
And the sin offering and guilt offering: for the sake of the sin.
Rabbi Yosei said:
Even one who did not have in his heart
any one of all these: it is valid,
because it is a stipulation of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs from the רישא and סיפא were rejected, the גמרא switches to a completely new source.
steps.raayaObject: That a זבח slaughtered סתמא, with no stated intent, is כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה on 46b: the six intentions and רבי יוסי's ruling

steps.title: What the court's stipulation was
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the תנאי בית דין: the court ruled that a person should not say 'לשמו', out of concern that he might end up saying 'שלא לשמו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית דין made a rule that a person should not say 'for its sake', because he might come to say 'not for its sake'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יוסי meant by 'a stipulation of the court'. This explanation sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the intention out loud is risky, because the person might slip and say the wrong one, and that would make the קרבן פסול. So בית דין told people to slaughter without saying anything. In other words, slaughtering סתמא became the standard practice.

keyTerms.meaning: They stipulated, they set a condition
For its own sake, with the correct intent
Not for its own sake, with the wrong intent

phrases.english: The court stipulated
phrases.notes: Now the גמרא is explaining רבי יוסי's words 'a stipulation of the court'.

phrases.english: that he should not say 'for its sake',
lest he come to say 'not for its sake'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְנוֹ בֵּית דִּין דְּלָא לֵימָא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'תנאי בית דין' quoted in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין instructed people not to state 'לשמו' when slaughtering, to avoid mistakenly saying 'שלא לשמו'.

steps.title: The court would never set up a practice that ruins the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the proof: if סתמא were פסול, בית דין would never tell everyone to slaughter that way. So סתמא is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you thought slaughtering without intent is invalid, would the court really go and set up a practice that makes the offering invalid?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows that the court's rule only makes sense if slaughtering סתמא is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court's rule meant people would slaughter without saying any intent. It is unthinkable that בית דין would require a practice that disqualifies קרבנות. So סתמא must be כשר, and this time the proof is not rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, you might think

steps.whatToRemember: זבחים slaughtered סתמא are כשר. The proof is that בית דין itself told people not to state 'לשמו', and the court would never set up a practice that ruins a קרבן.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that without specification it is invalid,
would the court arise and stipulate
something that makes it invalid?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the explanation of the court's stipulation to prove that סתמא is כשר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A זבח slaughtered סתמא is כשר, since בית דין would not mandate a practice that disqualifies offerings.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a גט written without intent is invalid?
steps.stepSummary: Now that זבחים are settled, the גמרא asks about the other half of the comparison: what is the source that a גט written סתמא is פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding a גט, where do we learn that if it was written without specification it is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finished with זבחים and now opens a new question about גט. This step sets up a search for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוגיא contrasts זבחים, where סתמא is כשר, with גט, where סתמא is פסול. Having found the source for זבחים, the גמרא now asks for the source on the גט side.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And regarding a bill of divorce,
that without specification it is invalid: from where do we know this?
phrases.notes: Here 'without specification' means it was written without having a particular woman in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the settled זבחים side of the comparison to the גט side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a גט written סתמא, without a specific woman in mind, is פסול.

steps.title: First attempt: the man who overheard scribes in the market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a source from a משנה in גיטין. A man overhears scribes reading out a גט with names that match his own, and the גט is פסול for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say the source is the משנה: a man walking in the market heard scribes reading out, 'So-and-so divorced so-and-so from such-and-such place,' and said, 'That is my name and my wife's name.' That גט is פסול for him to divorce with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer to the question from step 20. It brings a משנה where a גט not written for this specific man is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scribes did not write this גט for this particular man. So it looks like a סתמא גט, not written for his sake. Since the משנה says it is פסול, it seems a סתמא גט is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (it introduces a suggested proof that will probably be pushed off)
Scribes who write documents like a גט

phrases.english: If we say it is from that which we learned in a Mishnah:
A man was passing through the marketplace,
and heard scribes dictating:
"The man so-and-so divorces the woman so-and-so
from such-and-such place,"
and he said: "This is my name and that is my wife's name"
phrases.notes: He wants to take that same גט and use it for his own divorce.

phrases.english: it is unfit to divorce with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 20 about the source for a סתמא גט being פסול.
steps.raayaObject: That a גט written סתמא is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in גיטין about the man who overheard scribes reading a גט with matching names

steps.title: Rejected: those scribes were only practicing
steps.stepSummary: Using רב פפא, the גמרא pushes off the proof. Those scribes were practicing, so their גט was not written for divorce at all, which is worse than סתמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe that משנה follows רב פפא, who said: we are dealing with scribes who were practicing their writing, and the גט was not written for the purpose of divorce at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 21. That משנה is about a practice document, not a real סתמא גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A practice copy was never meant to divorce anyone, so of course it is פסול. A real סתמא גט is different: it is written to be used for divorce, just not for a named woman. That case might still be כשר, so the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (it introduces a pushback on a proof)
Cutting off; a word for divorce

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'not written for divorce at all' (a practice copy) with 'written סתמא' (written for divorce, but not for a specific woman). The whole rejection depends on these being two different cases.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is in line with רב פפא's explanation
as רב פפא says:
Here we are dealing with scribes who are used to practicing;
and it was not written for the sake of divorce at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 21 by redefining the case in that משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the רישא of the משנה in גיטין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is a practice document not written for divorce at all, so it says nothing about a real סתמא גט.

steps.title: Turning to the next part of that משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'rather, from this,' setting up a new proof from the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from this:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to bring a new proof from the next part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה failed because it could be about practice documents. So the גמרא moves to the next part, hoping to find a case of a גט truly written for divorce, but סתמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from this (it brings a new proof after the earlier one failed)

phrases.english: Rather, derive it from this:
phrases.notes: He means the next part of that same משנה, which comes right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rejection in step 22, introduces a replacement proof from the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a גט written סתמא is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The next clause (סיפא) of the משנה in גיטין, which is quoted at the start of the next amud
